module_title: Towards Independence (1939-1947) - Political Deadlock and Demand for Pakistan
introduction: This level explores the political stalemate following the Congress ministries' resignation, the methods of individual protest, the Muslim League's rigid stand on the Two-Nation Theory, and various political formulas (August Offer, C.R. Formula, Wavell Plan).

core_concepts.title: August Offer & Individual Satyagraha (1940)
core_concepts.description: Viceroy Linlithgow made the 'August Offer' in 1940. Congress rejected it, and Gandhi launched a limited 'Individual Satyagraha' to morally challenge the British war effort without causing mass disruption.

core_concepts.title: Lahore Resolution (1940)
core_concepts.description: On March 23, 1940, the Muslim League formally passed a resolution demanding a separate, sovereign state for Muslims (Pakistan).

core_concepts.title: C.R. Formula (1944)
core_concepts.description: C. Rajagopalachari proposed a formula to resolve the Congress-League political deadlock (suggesting a plebiscite in Muslim-majority areas after independence), but Jinnah rejected it.

core_concepts.title: Wavell Plan & Simla Conference (1945)
core_concepts.description: Viceroy Lord Wavell proposed reconstructing the Executive Council with equal representation of Caste Hindus and Muslims. The conference failed due to Jinnah's stubborn demand that the League must nominate *all* Muslim members.

core_concepts.title: Direct Action Day (1946)
core_concepts.description: Dissatisfied with the Cabinet Mission's proposals, the Muslim League called for 'Direct Action Day' on August 16, 1946, resulting in severe communal riots in Calcutta and Noakhali.

important_entities.name: Acharya Vinoba Bhave
important_entities.significance: Gandhi selected him to initiate the Individual Satyagraha in 1940 (Jawaharlal Nehru was the second).

important_entities.name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
important_entities.significance: Chief advocate of the Two-Nation Theory, who gave the slogan 'Divide and Quit'.

important_entities.name: Usha Mehta
important_entities.significance: Operated the secret Congress Radio during the Quit India Movement when all major leaders were arrested.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exams frequently ask for the exact order. 1st: Vinoba Bhave, 2nd: Jawaharlal Nehru, 3rd: Brahma Datt.
The term 'Pakistan' was not coined by Jinnah or Allama Iqbal. It was coined in 1933 by Chaudhary Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: P - Pethick-Lawrence, A - A.V. Alexander, C - Sir Stafford Cripps.

exam_strategy_tips: Master the exact chronological order: August Offer (1940) -> Cripps Mission (1942) -> C.R. Formula (1944) -> Wavell Plan (1945) -> Cabinet Mission (1946).
Remember that the Quit India Movement is also historically referred to as the 'August Kranti'.
